--- title: "Quickstart" --- A district has measured under-5 prevalence at 0.45, with pyrethroid resistance in the local vector population at 0.30 and the nets currently in use pyrethroid-only at 0.70 coverage. Biting is mostly on humans (`Q0 = 0.85`) and mostly in bed (`phi_bednets = 0.80`). Transmission is perennial, and there is no spraying. The next mass distribution is due, and the question is what effect switching those nets to pyrethroid-PBO would have. ## One scenario A `Scenario` is a single object holding one candidate campaign, describing both the setting as it is now and the intervention that switches on at the campaign. The seven fields before `eir_target` give the setting, the `py_*` fields give the current net mix, and the `*_future` fields give the campaign. `EirTarget(0.45, "prevalence")` tells `run_scenarios` that 0.45 is a measured prevalence and not an EIR. It is inverted into a baseline EIR before the emulator sees anything. ::: {#f15caeeb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from estimint import Scenario, EirTarget, run_scenarios pbo = Scenario( name="PBO switch", res_use=0.30, # pyrethroid resistance Q0=0.85, # share of bites taken on humans phi=0.80, # share of bites taken in bed seasonal=0.0, # 0 perennial, 1 strongly seasonal irs=0.0, # current IRS coverage eir_target=EirTarget(0.45, "prevalence"), py_only=0.70, # current nets: pyrethroid-only at 70% coverage itn_future=0.70, # the campaign: same coverage... net_type_future="pyrethroid_pbo", # ...different net ) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## Future coverage must be set explicitly `itn_future=0.70` is not "keep the nets you have", and if it is left out both `dn0_future` and `itn_future` are set to zero, which models the nets being **withdrawn** at the campaign rather than continuing. The same holds for `irs_future`, which does not inherit `irs`. Every intervention you want to persist past the campaign must be restated in its `_future` field, even when nothing about it changes. ::: ## Run it `run_scenarios` takes a list of scenarios, one here and hundreds later, and runs the whole pipeline for each of them. It converts net mix and resistance to `dn0`, converts prevalence to a baseline EIR, and then calls the emulator. It returns one row per scenario. ::: {#b465088c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} results = run_scenarios([pbo]) results.drop(columns=["prevalence", "cases"]).T ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
0
name PBO switch
input_mode prevalence
net py_only
net_future pyrethroid_pbo
dn0_use 0.311
itn_use 0.7
irs_use 0.0
dn0_future 0.48495
itn_future 0.7
irs_future 0.0
routine 0.0
lsm 0.0
seasonal 0.0
eir_baseline 31.960129
mosquito_delta 0.0
eir_final 31.960129
hbr_baseline NaN
hbr_new NaN
prev_y9 0.456028
prev_endline 0.470118
cases_endline 2.412444
``` ::: ::: Each row of that transposed column is one field of the result. `dn0_use` is the lethality of the nets in the ground today and `dn0_future` the lethality of the PBO nets replacing them, and since coverage is unchanged at 0.70 the switch between the two is the whole intervention. `eir_baseline` is the transmission intensity implied by a prevalence of 0.45 in this setting, in infectious bites per person per year. `prev_y9` is prevalence at the campaign, `prev_endline` three years after it, and `cases_endline` the clinical case rate there. `hbr_baseline` and `hbr_new` are `NaN`, because they are only computed when a prevalence input is paired with a non-zero `mosquito_delta`. This scenario perturbs nothing about mosquito density. ## The trajectory The two columns dropped from the table, `prevalence` and `cases`, are the trajectories. Each cell holds a 157-element NumPy array rather than a tidy long table. The grid is 157 windows of 14 days starting at day 2190, with the campaign at day 3285, and expressing it as years from the campaign puts zero where the nets change, giving three years of pre-campaign baseline followed by three years of response. ::: {#a6c7992a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np prev = results.loc[0, "prevalence"] abs_t = 2190 + 14 * np.arange(len(prev)) # day of each 14-day window years = (abs_t - 3285) / 365 # years from the campaign print(prev.shape, years[0].round(2), years[-1].round(2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (157,) -3.0 2.98 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#7c5b98ff .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4)) ax.plot(years, prev, color="#00d4aa", lw=2) ax.axvline(0, color="#8b93a3", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.7) ax.set_xlabel("Years from the campaign") ax.set_ylabel("Under-5 prevalence") ax.set_ylim(0, None) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Under-5 prevalence for a switch to pyrethroid-PBO nets at 0.70 coverage, in a setting with resistance 0.30 and a measured prevalence of 0.45. The dashed line marks the campaign.](quickstart_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){fig-alt='A line chart of prevalence against years from the campaign. Prevalence wanders between about 0.29 and 0.50 over the three years before the campaign and reaches 0.46 at it, then drops sharply to about 0.26 a year after the campaign before climbing back to about 0.47 by the end of the third year.'} ::: ::: Prevalence falls sharply once the PBO nets go out and reaches its minimum about a year later, then rises again over the rest of the horizon. The endline value on its own understates the campaign, since prevalence at three years is well above its minimum at one. The three years to the left of the line are not flat. Nor are they expected to be. `EirTarget` pins prevalence at the campaign, where `prev_y9` is 0.456 against the 0.45 that was measured, and what precedes it is the emulator's own history of the setting under the nets already in place. Whether PBO is worth the extra cost per net depends on the alternatives. One scenario cannot say. [Comparing campaigns](../06-scenarios/comparing.qmd) sets five options against each other in this same district: withdraw, replace like-for-like, PBO, pyrrole, and PBO plus IRS and LSM. ## Next - What EIR, HBR, prevalence and cases each mean: [EIR, HBR, prevalence, and cases](../03-concepts/equilibrium.qmd). - Where `dn0` comes from: [Nets and dn0](../04-estimint/nets-and-dn0.qmd). - Every field of `Scenario`, and a grid of them: [One call, end to end](../06-scenarios/run-scenarios.qmd). - Coming to Python from R: [Coming from R](coming-from-r.qmd).
